segments: The hundredth and first dynasty.
The Hun kings.

all the Christians in the Green Church dedicated to Mar Ahudemmeh,
which the Arabs had seized,
hid themselves,
and remained unharmed from the beginning of the Fast until Palm Sunday,
which was the seventeenth of Adar in the year 1569
of the Greeks [1258 AD].
Then a certain wicked Arab man named Bar Duri slandered the Christians before their governor (shiḥnah):
"These people have hidden many of the Arabs' possessions,
and their owners were killed,
yet they have not given you anything."
Now when the governor questioned the Christians about this,
they were unable to deny it,
but confessed and brought everything before him.
And he sent and informed the King of Kings,
and a sentence of death was issued against the wretched Tagritans,
according to the law of the Mongols.
And a great chief was sent,
and with him an army of Tatars;
and they began taking the Christians twenty by twenty,
bringing them up to the citadel as if to demolish it,
and killing them.
And they did so
until they had finished them off.
And no one escaped,
except for an old man or an old woman.
The sons and daughters, however, were carried off into captivity.
And the Arabs seized the Great Church once again.
And only two priests from Karme remained to pray in the rest of the churches with a few people who dwelt in it.
As for the slanderer Bar Duri,
a Christian man named Bahram, who became governor (shiḥnah) of Tagrit,
killed him.
And Badr al-Din, the lord of Mosul,
when he heard that Baghdad had been taken,
sent his man, Malik Salih, with a thousand horsemen,
ostensibly as aid to the King of Kings;
but he did not receive him well.
And he said to him:
"You were waiting to see who would be victorious,
so that you might attach yourselves to him.
And if the Caliph had conquered,
you would have gone to him and not to us."
And when Salih returned to his father Badr al-Din and informed him,
Badr al-Din trembled,
and he arose and took an unspeakably immense amount of wealth,
and went in person to the King of Kings,
and appeased him, and returned in peace,
though after great fear.
